newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada economy to pick up pace next year - report.
newsitem.headline: Canada economy to pick up pace next year - report.

text.p: Canada's economy, which suffered in 1996 from a sharp slowdown in export growth and an unexpected second-quarter decline in inventories, shows signs of rebounding in 1997, according to a report released on Thursday by the Conference Board of Canada.
The board's 1996 Canadian Outlook projects real GDP to grow by 1.5 per cent in 1996 and increase by 2.7 per cent in 1997.
The outlook, however, differs from province to province. Alberta and Saskatchewan will fare the best, while other parts of the country can expect slower growth, the board said.

"Fiscal restraint and a weak consumer demand continue to dampen growth in central Canada, and the completion of the Hibernia and Fixed-Link projects will limit growth in Atlantic Canada," said Paul Darby, the board's director of economic services.
Darby said that strong energy prices in Alberta and higher grain prices in Saskatchewan would keep the two prairie provinces at a higher level of economic growth.
Alberta's economy is expected to grow by 2.9 percent in 1996 and 3.2 percent in 1997. Saskatchewan's economy will grow by 2.9 percent this year and 2.3 percent in 1997, the board said.
